The scenario: Defendant Wang's wife made a police statement; Wang and his wife went to police station, tore up the statement, refused to cooperate, resisted police, causing police officer (Gao) injuries: multiple skin abrasions, rib fracture, light injury. So crimes: assault on police (or causing injury to police). In Chinese criminal law, assault on police is "妨害公务" (obstructing public duty) or "暴力抗拒执法" which is "妨害公务" (obstructing public officials). Also causing injury to police may be "故意伤害" (intentional injury) but the victim is a police officer performing duty, so the appropriate charge is "妨害公务". The facts: He resisted police, caused injury. So likely "妨害公务". Also maybe "故意伤害" because he inflicted injury intentionally? The law: If the act is to resist police, it's "妨害公务" (Article 277). If causing injury to police, also "妨害公务" includes causing injury. So we label "妨害公务". Also maybe "故意伤害" if the injury is intentional. But the description says he used violent resistance, causing injury. Usually the charge is "妨害公务" (obstructing public duty). The correction lessons didn't mention "妨害公务" but we have to use correct label. The example earlier: "危险驾驶;妨害公务" for a case where driver bit police. So they used both "危险驾驶" and "妨害公务". Here we have no other crime besides obstruction. So answer: [罪名]妨害公务<eoa>.
